help.title: About Snags
help.overview: A Snag is a defect / punch-list item on a unit. Closing snags is quality-gate work, not a sale action. Status is open → in progress → resolved, or rejected. Assign someone before starting work.

sections.title: What a snag holds
items: Unit (required), title (required), optional description, location on the unit, trade.
Reported by, assigned to, due date, resolved-at.
Photos, notes, root cause, cost impact.
Flags: warranty item, DLP (defects liability period).
Optional work package or variation order when construction is tracking the fix.

sections.title: Actions
items: Assign — only while open or in progress.
Start working — only from open, and only if someone is assigned; sets in progress.
Finish working — only from in progress; can attach photos/notes and moves to resolved.
Rejected is a status for items that will not be fixed as requested — not the same as resolved.

sections.title: On this page
items: Create snags from a unit or from this company-wide list.
Filter by unit, severity, status, assignee.
Open snags appear on Group dashboard KPIs.

sections.title: How it behaves
items: A snag does not freeze a sale. Handover processes may still require snags closed as a business rule.
Not a modification request (a change the client asked for) and not an inspection (a checklist visit).

sections.title: Related records
items: Unit. Optional work package / variation order. Inspections often precede or follow snags.
